marginal.def: Marginal analysis decides one more unit at a time: do one more when its marginal benefit (the extra benefit of that unit) is at least its additional cost.

utility.def: The satisfaction a consumer gets from consuming goods and services; total utility is the satisfaction from all the units consumed.

marginal-utility.def: The extra utility from consuming one more unit of a good (MU); it usually falls as more is consumed, which is diminishing marginal utility.

mu-per-dollar.def: Marginal utility divided by the price of the good (MU/P). A consumer maximizes utility by spending the whole budget so that MU/P is equal across goods.

sunk-cost.def: A cost that has already been paid and cannot be recovered; it is the same whatever is chosen next, so it does not change the best decision.

budget-constraint.def: The limit a consumer's income and the prices of goods place on what can be bought: total spending cannot exceed the budget.
